title: Should our town close its main road to cars on Sundays?
text:
Many Indonesian cities, including Jakarta and Malang, already close some of their busiest roads to motor vehicles on Sunday mornings. On these Car Free Days, the roads fill with walkers, cyclists, skaters and families. Now our town council is considering doing the same with Jalan Merdeka, our main road, every Sunday from 6.00 to 10.00. Is this a good idea? There are strong arguments on both sides.

Supporters say that a car-free morning is good for people’s health. Instead of sitting in traffic, families could walk, cycle or play games in the open air. Children who live in crowded neighbourhoods, with no garden or park nearby, would have a safe place to run around.

The air would also be cleaner. In cities that hold Car Free Days, measurements have shown less air pollution along the closed roads during those mornings. With fewer engines running, there would also be less noise, so people could hear each other talk and even hear the birds.

Supporters also argue that a car-free road brings a community together. Neighbours who usually rush past each other could stop and chat, and local groups could run dance shows, reading corners or recycling stalls.

However, not everyone is convinced. Some shop owners on Jalan Merdeka worry that customers will not be able to park nearby and will shop somewhere else instead. Drivers who need to cross town, such as delivery drivers and people going to work, would have to take longer routes, which could cause traffic jams on smaller streets.

There are also safety concerns. Ambulances and fire engines must always be able to reach people quickly, so the council would need to keep an emergency lane open at all times.

On balance, I believe the benefits are greater than the problems. Most of the worries can be solved with careful planning: emergency lanes can be marked, delivery times can be changed, and stalls on the road might even bring more customers to local shops. A three-month trial would allow the council to listen to everyone and find out whether the idea really works.

What do you think? The council will hold a public meeting at the town hall on 14 June, and everyone who lives in the town is welcome to share their views.

Fajar Nugroho, Class 6A
